question.text:
Granny gave away her entire collection of antique spoons to three people. Her daughter received $8$ more than a third of the total; her son received $8$ more than a third of what was then left; finally her neighbour received $8$ more than a third of what was then left.

  2. $12$

The given implementation of $A^{*}$ graph search may be incorrect!

Select all of the problems that the bugs may cause when executing graph search.

Note that the fringe is a priority queue.

Nodes are inserted into the fringe using the standard key for $\mathrm{A}^{*}$, namely $f=g+h$.

$h$ is a consistent heuristic.

function A* GRAPH SEARCH(problem)
    fringe ← an empty priority queue
    fringe ← INSERT(MAKE-NODE(INITIAL-STATE[problem]), fringe)
    closed ← an empty set
    ADD INITIAL-STATE[problem] to closed
    loop
        if fringe is empty then
            return failure
        end if
        node ← REMOVE-FRONT(fringe)
        if GOAL-TEST(problem, STATE[node]) then
            return node
        end if
        for successor in GETSUCCESSORS(problem, STATE[node]) do
            if successor not in closed then
                ADD successor to closed
                fringe ← INSERT(MAKE-SUCCESSOR-NODE(successor, node), fringe)
            end if
        end for
    end loop
end function
  1. The GetSuccessors function could be called multiple times on the same state.
  2. The algorithm is no longer complete.
  3. The algorithm could return a suboptimal solution.
  4. The implementation is incorrect, but none of the above problems will be caused.
